approval.rationale: Prospective design-only scope for independent review and merge before implementation. The registry status is not a review result or merge authorization; implementation requires this unchanged contract in its exact base.

identity.name: Market-bar atomic file publication v1
identity.purpose: Publish one complete new market-bar Raw/Curated Parquet or recovery lineage JSON without overwriting any destination, and clean only the temporary sibling created by that invocation.

implementation_bindings.rationale: The single unlink occurrence removes only the exact temporary sibling exclusively created and still owned by this invocation, before or after no-replace publication; the final path is never a cleanup target.

initiators: ParquetStore.write_raw and ParquetStore.write_curated for one explicit market-bar snapshot path

The bounded offline Raw replay service holding a named modern terminal source manifest with snapshot_binding_mode exactly REGISTERED_PER_SYMBOL, for one immutable lineage record belonging to a fresh recovery run
authority_boundary.mutation_owner: src/market_vault/storage/atomic_file.py::_write_file_no_replace owns creation, publication and temporary-file cleanup for one invocation.
forbidden_bypass_layers: Callers supply an intended new final path and complete serialization input, never a cleanup path or permission to replace an existing target.
No overwrite flag, same-content success, os.replace, overwriting rename, delete-then-publish, cross-filesystem fallback, or additional destructive primitive is authorized.
The helper does not modify Catalog rows, source evidence, existing manifests, existing lineage records, or another invocation's temporary files.

mutated_assets: One exclusively created unique temporary sibling whose name does not end in .parquet
One previously absent final file: a market-bar Raw/Curated path in the existing layout, or a recovery lineage JSON under the configured manifest directory
excluded_assets: Every pre-existing target, including identical bytes, corrupt files, directories, links and reparse points
Old Raw/Curated files, source manifests, old run and pair records, quality evidence, and old recovery records
Other temporary files, crash residue, quarantine, Canonical/Dataset artifacts, unrelated datasets and persistent cleanup

allowed_transitions.rationale: The completely serialized, flushed and closed owned temporary file is published by successful same-filesystem os.link(temp, final).
Any existing destination, including one that appears during publication, is strictly refused without content comparison or mutation.
Serialization, flush, path validation or publication failure prevents this invocation from committing a final file.

forbidden_transitions.rationale: A published final file cannot become writable staging or a rollback target.
A later cleanup or caller error does not undo physical publication; report the actual published state and retain the final file.
An existing target cannot be accepted, replaced or deleted to complete the refused invocation.

commit_point.durable_authority: Successful os.link of the complete closed owned temporary file to the exact previously absent sibling final path.
commit_point.success_authoritative_when: The no-replace primitive has published the complete file. File publication alone is not pair registration, run completion or a filesystem/Catalog transaction.

pre_commit: Partial serialization is confined to the owned temporary name; the final file remains absent unless another invocation publishes it. Crash residue is not consumed by Parquet globs or adopted by later calls.
post_commit: A complete final file may exist even if the caller did not receive success or temporary cleanup failed. Retain it and any unverified residue; never roll back by deleting the final file.
Atomic local publication is not a guarantee against storage hardware failure, power loss, or interruption of the separate pair/Catalog steps.

restorable: Handled failure may clean only the exact temporary file created by the current invocation while ownership and its regular non-reparse identity remain established.
non_restorable: No published file or old Catalog row is restored over, repaired, deleted or replaced. A cleanup failure preserves the final file and does not erase the original failure evidence.
interruption_detection: Report destination-exists, serialization/publication failure, and published-with-temporary-residue distinctly enough to avoid inferring rollback or successful run completion.

Raw-only, pair-unregistered or failed Catalog publication may be recovered only from a named modern terminal source manifest with status SUCCESS, PARTIAL or FAILED and snapshot_binding_mode exactly REGISTERED_PER_SYMBOL. Verify its exact Raw paths and consumed hashes, then replay offline into a fresh run. Legacy or unbound manifests, missing terminal evidence and stale lifecycle locks are refused; no old run is promoted or automatically unlocked.

same_request_retry: A new invocation may retry only while the final destination remains absent and must create its own new temporary file; it never adopts previous temporary residue.
completed_retry: Every existing destination is refused, even when its bytes would equal the requested output. This operation provides no idempotent-success mode.
conflicting_retry: Changed input at the same target is refused and preserves the existing target. An explicitly requested recovery replay creates a new run and new output paths.

lock_authority: os.link supplies atomic destination exclusion; an existence pre-check is not the no-overwrite guarantee. Temporary ownership comes from exclusive creation.
lock_scope: The helper owns one temporary file and one intended final path. Service collection and recovery retain the existing market-bar lifecycle lock; no additional lock framework or stale-lock reclamation is introduced.
under_lock_revalidation: Use existing local path checks for the intended parent, owned temporary object and final target; retain the temporary file's identity and refuse cleanup if its ownership or type is uncertain.
concurrent_behavior: If another publisher wins the destination race, os.link must refuse and the loser may clean only its own temporary file. Unsupported hard-link capability and other filesystem errors fail without an overwriting fallback.

identities: The exact final path, complete serialized input, exclusively created temporary object and common parent filesystem

For recovery, the named modern terminal source manifest and exact REGISTERED_PER_SYMBOL binding mode, consumed Raw paths and SHA-256 hashes, compatible request/source-schema facts, and fresh target run identity
drift_behavior: Reject relevant symlink/reparse or unverifiable path components before traversal or mutation. Path or temporary ownership drift authorizes neither publication nor cleanup of the uncertain object.
Recovery validates original Raw request/run metadata before assigning new run metadata; it does not discover substitute source files or change the original evidence.

authoritative_evidence: A successful no-replace publication of the complete intended file
Recovery run success additionally requires lineage publication, persisted-pair verification and registration, quality recording, and only then terminal record_run using the existing schemas
non_success_evidence: An existing target, partial or orphan temporary file, one-sided pair, unregistered files, or lineage record alone is not successful run completion.
integrity_binding: Publication links the fully serialized temporary file without reopening the final path for writing. Existing pair verification remains authoritative for Raw/Curated facts.

One immutable lineage JSON binds the new recovery run to the exact consumed source manifest and Raw hashes; the new run uses its actual recovery ingestion time and leaves old files and Catalog rows unchanged.

invalidation_triggers.rationale: This internal file primitive introduces no persistent UI plan or preview.

confirmation_invalidation.rationale: No overwrite or user-data deletion confirmation is exposed.

execution_policy: A recovery API/CLI invocation explicitly names source evidence and creates a new run; it does not grant authority over old files, old Catalog rows or stale locks.

lifecycle_unit: One complete local file published from an owned temporary sibling
partial_mutation: Only the temporary name may expose an incomplete write; the final name appears after complete serialization. Raw, Curated, lineage and Catalog records remain separate publications.
rollback_expectation: Clean only the current owned temporary file when safe. Published files remain immutable, and incomplete pair/run authority remains fail closed.

retained_dependents: All original snapshots, manifests, Catalog rows, old recovery records, crash residue and unrelated artifacts remain unchanged.
refused_cases: Every existing destination; unsupported no-replace capability; unsafe or unverifiable relevant paths; uncertain temporary ownership; recovery without modern terminal source evidence bound by snapshot_binding_mode exactly REGISTERED_PER_SYMBOL, including legacy, missing, null or unknown binding modes
unsupported_cases: Same-content reuse, old-run repair, legacy migration, automatic source discovery, OpenD access, automatic unlocking, garbage collection, recursive cleanup, schema changes and a distributed transaction framework

permanent_deletion.rationale: The one unlink removes only invocation-created temporary storage; no published or pre-existing user-data deletion feature is authorized.

implementation_tests: The later implementation inventory has exactly one path.unlink occurrence in src/market_vault/storage/atomic_file.py::_write_file_no_replace, owned by this unchanged BASE contract and no exemption.
Both market-bar writers refuse repeated targets for identical and different input while preserving the existing files; a publication race also preserves the winner.
Interrupted serialization leaves no final Parquet and no temporary file visible to Parquet readers; handled cleanup never touches pre-existing temporary files or published outputs.

Unsupported os.link capability, relevant link/reparse paths and unverifiable temporary ownership fail without overwrite or broader cleanup; a post-publication cleanup error preserves and identifies the committed final file.

Offline recovery through the bounded API/CLI handles source Raw-only, unregistered-pair and Catalog-publication failures by producing a verified new run while source hashes and old Catalog rows remain unchanged.

Recovery records exact source lineage before terminal run publication, records quality before record_run, and refuses legacy/unbound manifests, non-REGISTERED_PER_SYMBOL binding modes, missing terminal evidence, Raw identity/schema mismatch and stale locks without touching original data.
